records.title: verify-chain: the estate-wide walk is now platform-admin only; any member can still trigger an unbounded walk of their own organisation's chain
records.evidenceAtHead: server/routes/c2c/actions.ts:799-848: the handler checks resolvePlatformAdmin(req) at :807. A caller who is not a platform admin gets verifyTenantChainOnAdminScope(orgId) (:808) with scope 'organization', the break redacted by breakForTenant (:821) and no estate `tenants` count. Only a platform admin reaches the estate walk on the app_super_admin connection (:825-832). resolvePlatformAdmin (server/middleware/requirePlatformAdmin.ts:111) decides from PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS or an active platform_role_grants row, never from the membership role. server/services/audit/tenant-chain-verdict.ts:77-97 passes { tenantId: orgId } to verifyAuditChain, so chain.ts readChainRows (:634-702) adds `AND tenant_id = $1`. /api/decision-lineage/verify-chain has the same split (server/routes/decision-lineage.ts:188-222, DP-77). I ran `npx vitest run server/services/audit/__tests__/chain-head-on-demand.test.ts -t IAM-26`: 4 passed. They cover: the org-8 admin gets org 8 only; another org's break reads 'another organization'; a membership super_admin with no grant gets organisation scope; the platform admin gets the estate. What remains: readChainRows has no LIMIT or pagination. For a tenant with legacy (unsequenced) rows it also loads every other tenant's legacy rows as context (chain.ts:687-700). The route is mounted with authMiddleware only (server/bootstrap/register-inline-routes.ts:347) and has no limiter of its own beyond the generic /api limiter (server/startup/middleware.ts:59-60).
records.fixedBy: f97d49331 (2026-10-01, IAM-26) server/routes/c2c/actions.ts:799-848; f0209791a (DP-77) server/routes/decision-lineage.ts:188-222; shared verifier server/services/audit/tenant-chain-verdict.ts:77-97
records.remaining: 1. Any signed-in member, a viewer included, can still trigger an on-demand walk of their organisation's whole audit_logs chain on demand. The walk is unpaginated and runs on a super-admin-scoped connection, so request volume is limited only by the generic /api limiter. 2. If the organisation has legacy (unsequenced) rows, the walk also reads every other tenant's legacy rows (id, tenant_id, occurred_at, sha256_chain) into API memory. Nothing from those rows is returned, but the work is cross-tenant. A fresh pilot database writes no legacy rows (chain.ts:219-243 refuses a tenantless write outside vitest), so this applies only to a database migrated from before chain_seq. The estate-wide DoS and the metadata leak in the finding are closed.
records.severityRationale: The P1 core is closed in code and covered by a passing test: a viewer can no longer scan every tenant or read platform totals and other tenants' break hashes. What is left is resource use bounded by one tenant's own audit volume. A small pilot tenant will not notice it, and the ledger and document-history reads already run the same walk.
records.humanTestingNote: A tester sees nothing different. A non-admin calling GET /api/c2c/actions/verify-chain or opening the Decision Lineage surface (/api/decision-lineage/verify-chain) gets scope 'organization' and their own org's verdict only.
records.instructions:
1. On concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0), in server/routes/c2c/actions.ts, put a per-organisation limiter in front of router.get('/verify-chain', ...) at :799. Build it with createRedisRateLimiter (server/middleware/redisRateLimiter.ts:521) with perOrganization: true and one rule, for example 6 requests per 10 minutes per org. Platform admins get their own small allowance. Wire the same limiter on server/routes/decision-lineage.ts:227.
2. In server/services/audit/chain.ts, add `maxRows?: number` to VerifyAuditChainOptions (:629-632). In readChainRows (:634), first run a `SELECT count(*)` with the same WHERE clause. If the count exceeds maxRows, throw a new AuditChainTooLargeError instead of loading the rows. Fail closed: the error is never a partial verdict.
3. In server/services/audit/tenant-chain-verdict.ts verifyTenantChainOnAdminScope (:77), take an optional maxRows and pass it through. In actions.ts :808 and decision-lineage.ts chainVerdictFor (:203), pass a configured ceiling, for example AUDIT_CHAIN_ON_DEMAND_MAX_ROWS (default 250000). Map AuditChainTooLargeError to 503 { error: 'AUDIT_CHAIN_TOO_LARGE_FOR_ON_DEMAND', detail: 'The daily integrity sweep is the authoritative verdict for a chain this size.' }. Never return ok:true.
4. Keep the legacy-context read (chain.ts:687-700) only for platform admins. For a non-admin caller whose tenant has legacy rows, return the latest daily-sweep verdict for that org (server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts records it) or a 503 'verify on the operator path'. Do not walk other tenants' legacy rows on the caller's request.
5. Tests first, in server/services/audit/__tests__/chain-head-on-demand.test.ts next to the IAM-26 describe block (:342). (a) The seventh request from one org within the window gets 429. (b) A tenant whose row count exceeds maxRows gets 503 and the walk's SELECT of rows is never issued (assert on the mocked client's query log). (c) A non-admin in a tenant with legacy rows causes no query with `tenant_id IS DISTINCT FROM`. Run them against HEAD first and record the red, then implement.
records.acceptance: Each new test fails at HEAD before the change and passes after. The existing 4 IAM-26 tests still pass. A viewer's 7th request in the window returns 429. An over-ceiling tenant returns 503 AUDIT_CHAIN_TOO_LARGE_FOR_ON_DEMAND, never ok:true. A non-admin request issues no cross-tenant SELECT on audit_logs (asserted on the query log).
records.dependencies: None. The limiter is per task without Redis (SEC-08), so it holds across tasks only once ElastiCache exists.

records.title: Three live credentials still in git history (two Neon OWNER passwords, one Hugging Face token); the demo JWT is closed by code reasoning
records.evidenceAtHead: .gitleaksignore:15-42 still has three '# status: live — revoke (founder; P0-17)' blocks: the Neon OWNER password for ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4 (:15-27), the Neon OWNER password for ep-icy-brook-aha5br78 (:31-34), and the Hugging Face token in 3e1dcf8f0 (:38-42). Each still says there is no rotation record. `grep -c '^# status: live' .gitleaksignore` returns 3. The fourth block, the HS256 token in VaultMarketingPage.jsx (:44-58), is now 'not a secret'. Code backs that: both required authenticators call requireAccessTokenReason (server/middleware/tokenType.ts:98-104), which refuses any token without type 'access', and that token has no type, userId or organizationId. The leaked endpoint is still named as production in .devcontainer/devcontainer.json:17 (NEON_PROD_BRANCH=ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4-pooler) and .github/c2c-agent.yml:16. .github/workflows/neon-preview-db.yml creates PR branches in that Neon project, and a branch inherits the owner password. CI only warns: .github/workflows/ci.yml:2452-2457 prints '3 credential(s) ... recorded as live'. tests/ci/secret-history-scan.contract.test.ts:120 allows only live|public by design|not a secret, and :125-128 requires the INF-22 block to read 'live'. So the repo has no way to record a revocation yet.
records.fixedBy: 8fdfc74bd (2026-10-05): the demo JWT block in .gitleaksignore:44-58 is dispositioned 'not a secret'. The code basis is server/middleware/tokenType.ts:98-104. The commit also added a rotation runbook, which is a claim, not evidence.
records.remaining: The two Neon neondb_owner passwords (ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4, ep-icy-brook-aha5br78) and the Hugging Face token from 3e1dcf8f0 have no record of revocation. Repo files still treat ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4 as the production Neon branch, and preview branches cut from it inherit the leaked password. The contract test cannot express a revoked status. Only the founder can confirm whether the credentials were actually rotated in the Neon and Hugging Face consoles. The repo's own record says they were not.
records.severityRationale: The pilot's production database is AWS RDS (Terraform), not Neon, so these passwords do not open pilot customer data. That is why this is not P0. Still, an owner password for a project the repo labels production, plus a live HF token, is readable by anyone with the repository. A GxP buyer's security questionnaire asks about known unrotated credentials, and SOC 2 CC6.1 covers it. Fix before pilot users rely on the system. It needs no code, only founder console access.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot see this. One caution: if a staging or test environment points at the ep-wild-forest or ep-icy-brook Neon endpoints, anyone with the repo history can read the tester data there. Run human testing against the AWS staging stack or a freshly credentialed database.
records.instructions:
1. Founder, Neon console, project ep-frosty-salad-afl93crk (named in .devcontainer/devcontainer.json:16): reset the neondb_owner password on the branches behind ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4 and ep-icy-brook-aha5br78. Reset or delete every agent and preview branch cut from them (neon-preview-db.yml creates preview/pr-<n>). Update whatever consumes them (GitHub repo secrets and vars, local .env files) from a password manager. Never paste the values into the repo.
2. Founder, Hugging Face account settings, Access Tokens: revoke the token committed in 3e1dcf8f0 (test-api-key.js:8, test-embeddings.js:7). If a token is still needed, issue a new one into AWS Secrets Manager (terraform/stack/main.tf module "secrets").
3. Prove each old credential is refused, without printing it. Load it from `git show 3e1dcf8f0:test-api-key.js` and the fingerprinted Neon commits into a shell variable. Run `psql "$OLD_URI" -c 'select 1'` and expect 'password authentication failed'. Run `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OLD_HF" https://huggingface.co/api/whoami-v2` and expect 401. Save the redacted outputs as founder-attested evidence under docs/evidence/D6/<date>-p0-17-revocation/.
4. Engineering, failing first: in tests/ci/secret-history-scan.contract.test.ts:120, widen the status regex to `(live|revoked \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}|public by design|not a secret)`. Replace the :125-128 'INF-22 is live' assertion with one that says the INF-22 block is 'live' OR 'revoked <date>' with an evidence path on a '# evidence:' line. Add an assertion that a 'revoked' block without an '# evidence:' line fails. Run it and see it red on a mutated copy before changing .gitleaksignore.
5. In .gitleaksignore:15, :31 and :38, change '# status: live — revoke (founder; P0-17)' to '# status: revoked YYYY-MM-DD (founder; P0-17)' and add '# evidence: docs/evidence/D6/<date>-p0-17-revocation/'. Keep every fingerprint line: the full-history gitleaks job (ci.yml:2446-2449) needs them to stay green. Do not rewrite history (Rule 0).
6. Update .devcontainer/devcontainer.json:17 and .github/c2c-agent.yml:16 so they no longer name the leaked endpoint as production. Point them at the new branch, or remove the key if nothing reads it (grep NEON_PROD_BRANCH and production_branch first).
7. Confirm the warning step at ci.yml:2452-2457 reports 0 live and stays silent.
records.acceptance: `grep -c '^# status: live' .gitleaksignore` is 0. Every former live block reads 'revoked <date>' with an evidence path. The contract test fails on a mutated .gitleaksignore (a revoked block without evidence, or an unknown status) and passes on the real one. A connection with the old Neon password and a whoami call with the old HF token are both refused, with the redacted output on file. The CI 'Name the history credentials not yet revoked' step prints no warning. No repo config names ep-wild-forest-ahbojhu4 as production.
records.dependencies: Founder access to the Neon and Hugging Face consoles. Engineering steps 4-7 wait for steps 1-3.

records.title: Terraform production still has no WAF, GuardDuty, AWS Config, VPC flow logs, ALB access logs or CloudWatch alarms/SNS (RDS is now on a customer-managed KMS key)
records.evidenceAtHead: A case-insensitive grep across terraform/**/*.tf (tests excluded) for aws_wafv2|web_acl|guardduty|aws_config_|configuration_recorder|flow_log|cloudwatch_metric_alarm|aws_sns_topic|elasticache|waf|alarm|sns|redis finds no resource. The only hit is the comment at terraform/modules/cloudfront/main.tf:149-156: 'No WAF yet: a founder decision, not defaulted', with #trivy:ignore:AWS-0011 on the distribution. ALB access logs are still off: terraform/modules/alb/variables.tf:40-43 defaults access_logs_bucket = "", alb/main.tf:41-44 enables logging only when that is set, and module "alb" in terraform/stack/main.tf:363-374 does not pass it. terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf:4 aws_vpc.this has no aws_flow_log. CloudTrail with CloudWatch Logs and CMK is present (terraform/modules/compliance-evidence/main.tf:262-351). The audit-chain sweep's incident alert (server/jobs/auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:484-497 calling reportSecurityAlert) reaches an operator only through SECURITY_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL (server/services/security-alerts.ts:15). Neither terraform/ nor .github/workflows/deploy-aws.yml provisions that variable, so in production it is a console line no alarm watches. Fixed since the audit: the RDS instance, its snapshots and Performance Insights now use aws_kms_key.database and the task secrets use aws_kms_key.secrets (terraform/stack/database_keys.tf:36-57; main.tf:119, :357).
records.remaining: 1. No WAFv2 web ACL on CloudFront, so no managed rules and no edge rate rule. 2. No GuardDuty detector. 3. No AWS Config recorder or rules. 4. No VPC flow logs. 5. No ALB access logs. 6. No CloudWatch alarms or SNS topic, so 5xx bursts, unhealthy targets, RDS pressure, auth-failure spikes, CloudTrail CIS events and the daily audit-chain sweep incident alert nobody. 7. SECURITY_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL is not provisioned. Redis/ElastiCache is still absent too, tracked under SEC-08. Of the original evidence, only the RDS-default-KMS sub-point is closed (5ef2787a5).
records.severityRationale: For one small FDA-only pilot the missing WAF is a founder cost decision that can wait if it is recorded. But with no alarms and no forwarding for the audit-integrity alert, a Part 11 audit-chain break or an outage in production would go unseen until a user reports it. GuardDuty, flow logs and ALB logs are the minimum an incident responder and a GxP vendor-qualification questionnaire expect. All of this must exist before pilot users rely on production. None of it blocks starting the pilot on a non-production stack.
records.humanTestingNote: Testers cannot see this on a local or staging deployment. If staging comes from this Terraform, operators have no alarm on 5xx or the audit sweep, so a failed request a tester hits is visible only in CloudWatch Logs. Pull logs manually when a tester reports an error.
records.instructions:
1. Founder: record the WAF decision (cost about $5/month plus $1 per rule per month plus per-request fees). Recommended: on, with AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet's SizeRestrictions_BODY overridden to COUNT, so Vault uploads and AnA turns over 8 KB are not blocked.
2. On concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0), add terraform/stack/detective_controls.tf with: (a) aws_guardduty_detector "this" { enable = true }, plus aws_guardduty_detector_feature for S3_DATA_EVENTS, RDS_LOGIN_EVENTS and RUNTIME_MONITORING (ECS Fargate agent management). (b) An AWS Config IAM role (managed policy AWS_ConfigRole), aws_config_configuration_recorder (all supported resources), aws_config_delivery_channel to module.evidence's bucket under prefix 'config/', aws_config_configuration_recorder_status enabled, and managed rules: s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited, s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only, rds-storage-encrypted, rds-instance-public-access-check, cloudtrail-enabled, restricted-ssh, vpc-flow-logs-enabled. (c) aws_sns_topic "ops_alarms" with kms_master_key_id = aws_kms_key.secrets.arn and an email subscription from a new variable alarm_email (required when environment == "production"; validate in variables.tf). (d) aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm resources on the ALB (HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count, HTTPCode_ELB_5XX_Count, UnHealthyHostCount, TargetResponseTime p95), on RDS (CPUUtilization, FreeStorageSpace, DatabaseConnections) and on ECS service CPU and memory, all with alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.ops_alarms.arn]. (e) aws_cloudwatch_log_metric_filter plus alarms on the API log group (terraform/modules/ecs-fargate/main.tf:18 aws_cloudwatch_log_group.api; export its name as a module output if it is not one already) for the patterns "AUDIT INTEGRITY FAILURE" (auditChainIntegritySweep.ts:486) and "[SECURITY]" (security-alerts.ts:33), and on the CloudTrail log group (compliance-evidence main.tf:277) for the CIS events: root login, IAM policy change, KMS key disable/schedule-deletion, security-group change, console sign-in failures.
3. In terraform/modules/compliance-evidence/main.tf, extend aws_s3_bucket_policy.evidence (:231) with the AWSConfigBucketPermissionsCheck and AWSConfigBucketDelivery statements, scoped to the 'config/' prefix and this account (aws:SourceAccount).
4. In terraform/modules/vpc-secure/main.tf, add aws_flow_log on aws_vpc.this (:4), traffic_type ALL, to a KMS-encrypted aws_cloudwatch_log_group with retention_in_days >= 365 and an IAM role for flow-log delivery.
5. ALB access logs: in terraform/stack/main.tf, add an S3 bucket for ALB logs (SSE-S3/AES256, because ALB log delivery does not support SSE-KMS), with block-public-access, a bucket policy admitting logdelivery.elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com (or the region's ELB account) to PutObject under AWSLogs/<account>/, and a lifecycle expiration that matches the retention policy. Pass access_logs_bucket = <that bucket>.id in module "alb" (:363-374).
6. WAF, if the founder approves: add an aws provider alias for us-east-1. Add aws_wafv2_web_acl with scope = "CLOUDFRONT" and the rules AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet (SizeRestrictions_BODY set to count), AWSManagedRulesKnownBadInputsRuleSet, AWSManagedRulesAmazonIpReputationList, and a rate_based_statement (for example 2000 requests per 5 minutes per IP). Add aws_wafv2_web_acl_logging_configuration to an 'aws-waf-logs-<short>' log group. Add a web_acl_id variable to terraform/modules/cloudfront/variables.tf and set it on aws_cloudfront_distribution.this. Remove the #trivy:ignore:AWS-0011 line and the 'No WAF yet' comment (cloudfront/main.tf:149-156) in the same change.
7. Provision SECURITY_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL as a Secrets Manager secret in module "secrets" (main.tf:116) and inject it into the API and worker task definitions. Alternatively, rely on the metric-filter alarm from step 2(e) and record that decision. Either way, the sweep incident must page someone.
8. Failing first: add terraform/stack/tests/detective_controls.tftest.hcl (mock providers, as in boot_contract.tftest.hcl). Assert that the GuardDuty detector, Config recorder and status, VPC flow log, ALB access_logs.enabled == true, the SNS topic, the 'AUDIT INTEGRITY FAILURE' metric filter with its alarm, and (when enable_waf) the web ACL association all exist. Run `terraform test` in terraform/stack at HEAD and record it red, then implement until green. .github/workflows/terraform-tests.yml:44-80 runs it in CI.
9. Run the Trivy config scan and ci:trivy-inline-ignores so the removed ignore and the new resources pass.
records.acceptance: terraform/stack/tests/detective_controls.tftest.hcl fails at HEAD and passes after the change, and runs in terraform-tests.yml. `terraform plan` for staging shows the GuardDuty detector, Config recorder and rules, VPC flow log, the ALB with access_logs enabled, the SNS topic with alarms, and the WAF web ACL attached to CloudFront (if approved). After apply on staging: `aws guardduty create-sample-findings` produces a finding; forcing a 5xx burst triggers the ALB 5xx alarm email; logging the line 'AUDIT INTEGRITY FAILURE in test' from the API task triggers the metric-filter alarm; ALB log objects appear in the bucket within 5 minutes; a request over the rate rule from one IP gets 403 from CloudFront.
records.dependencies: Founder decisions on WAF cost and on the alarm recipient (email, PagerDuty or Slack). AWS account access for a staging apply. Shares infra work with SEC-08 (ElastiCache/REDIS_URL) and the infra lane's deploy-preflight changes.

records.title: Unkeyed request-read tables: all 101 remaining entries are classified (31 global, 51 derived, 19 exempt), and 0 are unreviewed
records.evidenceAtHead: scripts/ci/unkeyed-request-tables-baseline.json at HEAD has total 101. Counted by first word: 31 global, 51 derived, 19 exempt, 0 unreviewed. At 92ccdba1 it was 112: 103 unreviewed, 6 global, 3 derived. I ran `node scripts/ci/check-unkeyed-request-tables.mjs` and `... --unreviewed`, and both exit 0: '1082 tables created; 594 read by a per-request path; 101 of those carry NO tenant column; 101 baselined, 0 still unreviewed'. Spot-checks against migrations and code: chat_messages is in the parent-scoped spec (db/migrations/20260813_child_table_parent_scoped_rls.sql:178, chat_threads.organization_id; the file is CHILD_TABLE_PARENT_SCOPE at scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:84). capa_records and q_submissions are in the same spec (8 and 12 references). clinical_ops.* children have FORCE RLS and parent-EXISTS policies (db/migrations/20260902_clinical_ops_schema.sql:240-262). knowledge_documents 'exempt' holds: server/sage-plus-service.ts is imported only by server/routes/health.ts:12, and only for healthCheck. Production runs RLS_ENFORCE=on (terraform/stack/main.tf:243, asserted in terraform/stack/tests/boot_contract.tftest.hcl:183,652). Triage also found and fixed a live cross-tenant read, /api/graphrag/citation-trace (server/routes/graphrag.ts). I ran `npx vitest run server/routes/__tests__/graphrag-citation-trace-scope.test.ts`: 3 passed. audit.tamper_proof_log, one of the audit's named examples, is no longer in the read set (removed in 1bb92a71d).
records.fixedBy: a5bc45b71 (19 classified by parent-scoped spec), 31d9a9c5b (citation_chains live cross-tenant read fixed, server/routes/graphrag.ts + server/routes/__tests__/graphrag-citation-trace-scope.test.ts), b1b2f2c5b (all 105 carry a decision), fa8c212e5 (capa_records and q_submissions added to db/migrations/20260813_child_table_parent_scoped_rls.sql), 15af6bc4b, 93992487f (105 -> 101; DYNAMIC_KEYERS in scripts/ci/check-unkeyed-request-tables.mjs)
records.severityRationale: The finding's acceptance from WO-8 ('the unreviewed count in the baseline reaches 0 with per-table evidence') is met and checked by running the gate. Spot-checked derived and exempt reasons match migrations and imports at HEAD. Optional hardening, not part of the finding: the --unreviewed mode runs only in the nightly strict job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:2511), so a new 'unreviewed' entry written by --write-baseline would pass per-PR CI. Promoting ci:unkeyed-request-tables:unreviewed into the per-PR lint step beside ci.yml:686 would lock the zero in. The 'exempt because unmounted' entries (knowledge_documents, submission_projects/tasks, conversation_os_*) also have no gate tied to mount status.
